as_written_in_papers.quote: The proband (III-1) and three of the four cousins (III-2, III-4, III-5) had Danon disease caused by a missense mutation, c.1150 G > C, leading to an amino acid change (p.Gly384Arg) in splice variant B (exon 9B) of the LAMP2 gene (reference sequence NM_013995.1; nomenclature according to http://www.hgvs.org/Mutnomen/).

cases.statement: Four affected males of one Dutch family (III-1 proband, III-2, III-4, III-5), all carrying the variant and all with muscle weakness; two (III-1, III-5) had cone-rod dystrophy; III-5 also had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Zygosity is not stated; all are male.

people.label: III-1
people.key_phenotypes: cone-rod dystrophy from age 49 with bull's eye maculopathy, central scotoma and reduced cone and rod ERG; muscle weakness from 64 progressing to wheelchair dependency; no cardiomyopathy or mental retardation in Table 1

Fundus examination revealed a bull’s eye maculopathy and a peripheral salt-and-pepper retinopathy

phenotype_specificity.statement: Muscle weakness in all four carriers and cardiomyopathy in one; the eye phenotype (cone-rod dystrophy) is the new feature reported. RPGR was sequenced to exclude another cause of X-linked cone-rod dystrophy and was negative in the cousins with CRD. No other genes for the myopathy are reported as tested.

quotes.quote: Direct sequencing of the entire coding regions and flanking sequences of the genes LAMP2 and RPGR was performed at the Netherlands Institute of Neurosciences.
No RPGR mutations were found in the cousins with CRD (Fig. 1a).
Table 1: Clinical characteristics of the four relatives with Danon disease and a mutation in the LAMP2 gene

The presence of protective environmental factors in the non-affected siblings which prohibit lysosomal degradation, or a still unidentified mutation in another gene that explains CRD, are possible explanations.

segregation.statement: Four affected male carriers in one family; one unaffected male cousin (III-3) tested and did not carry the variant. Daughters of III-4 appeared unaffected and the daughter of III-5 died suddenly at 29 of cardiomyopathy; neither was reported as tested. No female carriers were tested.

quotes.quote: One cousin was unaffected (III-3), and had no LAMP2 mutation.
His two daughters appeared to be non-affected.
The daughter of this patient suddenly died at the age of 29 due to cardiomyopathy.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: On the batch transcript NM_002294.3 (LAMP2A) the variant is intronic (c.1093+2493G>C, p.?); on the paper's NM_013995.1 (LAMP2B) it is a missense change in exon 9B, p.Gly384Arg. The authors propose that only the LAMP2B isoform is affected and that residual protein explains the late onset.

quotes.quote: Gly384Arg is located in the coding sequence for splice variant LAMP2b, jeopardizing function of only this specific isoform.
The family of this report carried a recently identified missense mutation (p.Gly384Arg) in exon 9 of the LAMP2 gene, allowing formation of the protein [8].
The late onset of the two affected cousins in our family could be explained by the presence of this residual LAMP2 protein.

authors_classification.statement: The authors call p.Gly384Arg the causal mutation.

quotes.quote: The causal mutation was p.Gly384Arg in LAMP2; no mutations were found in RPGR.
It remains intriguing why not all family members with a pathogenic mutation in the LAMP2 gene developed CRD.

concerns: Transcript: the paper numbers the variant on NM_013995.1 (LAMP2B isoform, exon 9B) as c.1150G>C p.Gly384Arg; the batch maps it to NM_002294.3 (LAMP2A) as intronic c.1093+2493G>C with p.?. The protein_check flags the difference. The panel should assess it on the LAMP2B transcript.

Possible earlier report of the same family: the paper calls p.Gly384Arg 'recently identified' and cites reference [8] (van der Kooi 2008, PMID 18413590) for it and for III-1's muscle history. That paper is not in this batch; persons there may duplicate these four.

Relationships contradict each other: the Results call III-2, III-4 and III-5 cousins of the proband III-1; the abstract calls three of them siblings ('Two siblings had no ocular phenotype. The third sibling and a cousin developed CRD'); the Figure 1 legend calls the two with CRD 'two affected siblings', although Table 1 gives CRD to III-1 and III-5.
Zygosity is never stated; all four carriers are male.
The paper raises the possibility of another gene contributing to CRD in two carriers.
notes_for_panel: One family with four affected male carriers and one non-carrier unaffected male; late-onset myopathy is the shared feature. The variant's position relative to the LAMP2A transcript is the key question.
